name: Iseltal
kurzbeschreibung: The Iseltal in Osttirol is home to the Isel, the last free-flowing glacial river in the Alps, the Natura 2000 protected area, and the 73 km Iseltrail.
oeffnungszeiten: Ganzjährig 24/7 frei und kostenlos zugänglich; beste Wandersaison Mai–Okt
beschreibung:
Overview

The Iseltal is the primary geographical and ecological lifeline of Osttirol. It stretches from the glaciated three-thousand-metre peaks of the Venediger- and Glocknergruppe in the Nationalpark Hohe Tauern across roughly 57 kilometres to the confluence of the Isel into the Drau near the Dolomite town of Lienz at 673 metres above sea level. As one of the most scenically captivating valleys in the Eastern Alps, it shelters a natural monument of continental significance: the Isel is the last remaining completely free-flowing, unregulated glacial river in the entire Alpine arc, forming the backbone of a unique wild river landscape.

Wild River Landscape & Iseltrail

Owing to its outstanding ecological integrity, the river system of the Isel and its tributaries Schwarzach, Kalserbach, and Tauernbach was designated as a European Natura 2000-Schutzgebiet in 2015 and 2018 respectively. The dynamic bedload riverbed with gravel banks and sand islands provides a habitat for highly endangered alpine pioneer plants, above all the rare Deutsche Tamariske (Myricaria germanica), as well as endangered bird and fish species such as the common sandpiper and brown trout. For hikers, the spectacular Iseltrail was inaugurated in 2020: the approximately 73.5-kilometre long-distance hiking trail leads upstream from Lienz in five day stages through the Iseltal, Virgental, and Umbaltal to the arctic glacier snout of the Umbalkees at almost 2,500 metres above sea level. Along the route, hikers experience roaring whitewater, dramatic gorges such as the Umbalfälle, and tranquil riparian forests. Furthermore, the Isel is renowned internationally as a mecca for demanding whitewater sports (kayaking, rafting, and packrafting).

Visit & Getting There

The Iseltal and the walking trails along the river course are freely and openly accessible year-round free of charge; the best time for hiking and nature observation is from May to October. Rafting and kayaking tours are offered by professional outdoor companies in Lienz and Matrei from June to September (half-day tours from approx. €55.00 to €75.00). Arrival by car: from the north via the Felbertauernstraße B108 directly through the Iseltal; from the east and south via the Drautalstraße B100 to Lienz. By public transport: ÖBB trains to Bahnhof Lienz, from where VVT bus routes 951/952 (Iseltaler Tälerbusse) run hourly throughout the entire Iseltal via St. Johann im Walde and Huben to Matrei in Osttirol and onward to Prägraten am Großvenediger.

Tips

Substantial sections of the Iseltal-Radweg (R12) cycle path as well as the riverside promenades near Lienz and St. Johann im Walde are asphalted or surfaced with fine gravel, making them ideally suited for barrier-free excursions with pushchairs and wheelchairs. Be sure to plan a stop at the spectacular Umbalfälle, where a barrier-free viewing trail opens up direct vistas into the roaring glacial chasms.
